decision.fail_means: R5_NO_MEANINGFUL_OVERLAP_HEADROOM: the direction is closed before evaluation; the evaluation is never opened

estimator.differs_from_phase1a_draft: experiments/R5-01-ets-implementation/ets_trace.py metrics_from_log (never used to compute an H) clips T_tail to the union of all threads' wait windows and lets synchronous reads extend the tail; both can exceed the critical-path wait. headroom.py is the Phase 1b estimator; the draft is not used for G2.
estimator.independent_review: an independent reviewer challenged bound validity, double counting, causality, tracing bias, critical path, endpoint consistency and outcome dependence before acquisition; the 4 material findings (critical-wait thread choice, thread-id rule, readiness binding, rerun policy) were resolved; a second review found 2 more (flag-2 gate reads shrinking H; a seen-then-interrupted slot being rerun and overwritten), resolved by the issue-time rule above and the rerun rules below; the second reviewer then ACCEPTED, and its one residual minor gap (raw trace on disk before it is logged) was closed by trace_received and the traces/ accounting
operational_choices: critical-path wait interval of the first node = [wait_start, wait_end] of the thread whose wait ENDS LAST (ties -> the longer wait): the node cannot exit before that thread, so only that interval is on the critical path. first_node_wait = the maximum over threads of wait_end - wait_start; invariant H_layer <= first_node_wait (asserted)

c_first = latest completion of a read of the first node's kind issued at the first node (or the critical wait start if there is none); c_all = latest completion of a read issued at the first node that is not flagged SYNCHRONOUS (4), FALLBACK (8) or SYNC_IN_ISSUE (16); T_tail = max(0, min(c_all, wait_end) - max(c_first, wait_start))
W = max(0, min hook_in of the layer's last expert node - max hook_out of the first node): the compute window in which the deferred reads could at best be hidden

H_layer = min(T_tail, W); exactly one value per decode layer event, so overlapping or simultaneous reads are never summed (read/read overlap is not read/compute overlap); the union of all threads' wait windows is never used

reads issued at the first node = I records of the layer whose issue time lies in the first node's window [min hook_in, max hook_out]; every read must be attributable to exactly one node window, else the trace is invalid

reads flagged 4, 8 or 16 never extend the tail (paid synchronously, never hideable); a bounded completion (flag 2, recorded time = an upper bound) is taken at its optimistic end on each side: the recorded time for c_all and the issue time for c_first, so a late poll never shrinks H

thread identity: every node has exactly 12 T records with 12 distinct thread ids, the same id set in every node; every I record's thread id is in that set (arx_thread_id is shared by a thread's T and I records; ids need not start at 0)
decode tokens = decode graphs of the trace (router records with n_tokens = 1) and must equal predicted_n - 1 = 511
H = (sum over the 8 launches of sum H_layer, in ms) / (sum over the 8 launches of predicted_ms): the share of the measured decode time (WORKLOADS decode_metric_source) that is at best hideable
G2: H >= 1/25 in exact rational arithmetic (inclusive at exactly 4%)
every per-launch H fraction is reported with the pooled H; only the pooled H decides
telemetry is validated (pass/fail only, no H) right after every launch, warmup included, so an invalid trace stops the acquisition at once instead of after 9 launches
estimator.telemetry_fail_closed: unparseable records, wrong schema or arm, missing thread records, incoherent records, failed or unattributable reads, missing first node, single-node events, decode-graph mismatch, truncated or undecodable files: no H is computed

frozen_texts_quoted.G2_headroom: one-shot: H from the 8 pre-declared B launches on the frozen binary >= 0.04. Otherwise R5_NO_MEANINGFUL_OVERLAP_HEADROOM and the evaluation is never opened. H is not recomputed.
frozen_texts_quoted.IMPLEMENTATION_FREEZE: before G2: source hashes, binary hash, model and store hashes, and the list of implementation choices (wait primitive, handle-release point, barrier placement, pin-release point, touch order, trace record layout) are frozen; no change afterwards; every development timing comparison run before the freeze is appended to a committed development log
anti_rescue: only R5_POSITIVE_RUNTIME_IMPROVEMENT may be described as an improvement; every other label is reported as a negative or uninterpretable outcome, never as a partial success
no secondary endpoint, subset, prompt, budget, thread count or tracing configuration can upgrade the classification
no second scheduler variant, no parameter, no new prompt and no new budget after the freeze
the oracle bound H is never reported as an achievable gain
the evaluation is opened once; reruns only under blame_rules
no optional stopping: block counts are constants of this contract
no outlier removal, imputation, reordering or data-driven exclusion
frozen_texts_quoted.critical_path_rule: Every per-node time is taken on the critical path: a node starts when the first thread enters the hook and its store phase ends when the last thread leaves the hook (max over threads); a per-node wait is the maximum over threads of that thread's wait in that node. Thread 0 alone, means over threads and sums over threads are never used for a mechanism endpoint.

headroom_bound_H.definition: for every decode layer event: T_tail = time from the latest completion (over threads) of a first-node-kind read to the latest completion of any read issued at the first node, clipped to the first node's critical-path wait interval; W = gap from the last thread leaving the first node's hook to the first thread entering the hook of the layer's last expert node; H_layer = min(T_tail, W). H = sum of H_layer / decode tokens, expressed as a fraction of the mean decode ms/token of the same 8 launches.
headroom_bound_H.interpretation: an optimistic, loose upper bound on what moving the wait can hide (ignores interference); an opening gate only, never a result
headroom_bound_H.source: computed ONCE, after the implementation freeze, from exactly 8 B launches (each of the four development prompts twice) at 1.5 GiB on the frozen binary; every H value ever computed in R5 is reported

frozen_texts_quoted.host_conditions: AC power; same Windows power plan; background applications closed; Defender scheduled scans and Windows Update paused for the campaign; host record per launch (INSTRUMENTATION.json); no data-driven exclusion

launch.ignore_eos_why: evaluation prompts cannot be inspected in advance; without it an early end-of-sequence would make predicted_n < 512 and invalidate every arm by design
launch.process: one fresh server process per launch
launch.threads_why: EXP-027: 12 generation threads were the fastest measured setting for the 30B model; fixed, never tuned in R5

frozen_texts_quoted.model_identity: file SHA-256 of gguf and psxs recorded at the implementation freeze and checked at every launch
frozen_texts_quoted.phase1b: one-shot headroom gate G2 from 8 pre-declared B launches on the frozen binary
frozen_texts_quoted.threshold_justification_H: twice the MEI; realised hiding is a fraction of this optimistic bound, so below 4% there is no realistic way to pass the primary gate. Failing it only closes the direction early.
frozen_texts_quoted.warmup_convention: one uncounted launch per campaign with the first arm of block 1 and the identical environment, then 60 s cooldown; recorded, never used

outputs.disk_estimate: raw trace about 0.24 GB per launch (G1 traced B launch: 236 MB), one at a time; kept gzip traces about 35-60 MB each (ratio about 0.15-0.25 on real-format traces), about 0.3-0.5 GB for 8; logs about 1 MB. 2 GB free required.
outputs.duration_estimate: ESTIMATE: about 4-5 min per launch (G1 averaged 2.5 min per launch; plus tracing, model/store hashing before every launch, trace structure and gzip, cooldown) x 9 launches, plus about 5 min for the one-shot analysis: roughly 45-75 min in total

R5 runtime SHA-256 = IMPLEMENTATION_FREEZE = host_conformance R5_AUTHORIZED
development prompts only (evaluation ids are refused)

question: Does the frozen R5 runtime's baseline (arm B: layer wait, traced) leave enough expert-transfer wait on the decode critical path, hideable behind the compute that follows the first expert node of each layer, to justify opening Phase 2? Operationally: is the optimistic bound H >= 4% of decode time (G2)?

schedule.arm: B = ARGINE_EXPERT_WAIT=layer (explicit), ARGINE_RESEARCH_TRACE on, ARGINE_PREFETCH=0, asincrono, direct I/O
schedule.invalid_launch: the acquisition stops (no H). R5-00 blame_rules: a failed B launch is attributed to the campaign; one rerun of that slot only with --rerun-infrastructure CAUSE (power, windows-update-or-defender, disk-full, operator-interruption) --evidence FILE (hashed into the log); a second failure of the same slot aborts the campaign and G2 stays undecided. A counted trace is kept under an attempt-numbered name and its hash logged before any post-launch work; an attempt interrupted after that point cannot be rerun for operator-interruption; every superseded kept trace is reported in G2_RESULT (never deciding), and a missing or altered one blocks the gate. A trace_received record is logged as soon as the runtime's raw trace is handed over (interruptions from then on count as after the trace); a raw trace left in traces/ is analyzed and reported (never deciding), and any other unaccounted file blocks the gate. An attempt without a launch record counts as a failure. Every (re)start begins with a fresh uncounted warmup. A campaign marker in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Argine\r5 refuses a second output directory.
schedule.launch: one fresh server process per launch; 512 greedy tokens (ignore_eos, temperature 0, top_k 1, seed 42), 12 threads, context 4096 (host_conformance.py run_launch, unchanged)
schedule.per_launch_checks: model and store SHA-256 against the IMPLEMENTATION_FREEZE before the first launch of every (re)start and after every launch; AC power before every launch and in the host record after it (unknown = stop); host record before and after; telemetry validation; launch validity (512 tokens, graceful shutdown, one counter record, explicit layer arm, prefetch 0, budget, 0 violations / pending / drain / deferred reads, trace structure complete, 511 decode graphs)
schedule.warmup: 1 uncounted B launch with code-dev-1 (SCHEDULE warmup convention), structure recorded, trace deleted, never used; then 60 s cooldown

scope: development prompts only; one-shot; no scheduler variant; no Phase 2 artifact; H is never an achievable gain
